title: Why Government? Foundations of the Republic

questions.prompt: Crenshaw opens with which fundamental civics question?
choices: A Which party should ban elections?
B Why do we even have a government?
C How to abolish all law?
D Who invented the filibuster first?
questions.explain: He starts from why government exists if civilization restarted.

questions.prompt: In the Declaration language he unpacks, governments derive just powers from:
choices: A Divine right of kings alone.
B The consent of the governed.
questions.explain: Consent of the governed is packed into that sentence he quotes.

questions.prompt: Madison's case, as Crenshaw presents it, favors a republic over pure democracy because:
choices: A Pure democracy never fails historically.
B Representation over a large citizenry checks instability and factional passion.
questions.explain: He recounts the indictment of pure democracy and the case for a republic of representatives.

choices: B Both a House and a Senate as a check on public passions.
questions.explain: Bicameral = House + Senate checking an excitable public.

questions.prompt: Besides executive and legislative, the founders created which third branch?
questions.explain: He introduces the judicial branch as the third.
